Define a configurable state taxonomy

Source: R/taxonomy.R
ssf_taxonomy.Rd

Labels are assigned in increasing order of a fitted state signature. A rule can then check separate movement, selection, or transition contrasts. The same numerical and occupancy checks as in the guided workflow apply.

Usage

ssf_taxonomy(
  name,
  labels,
  formula = ~step + log_step + cos_angle,
  order_by = "mean_step",
  rules = NULL
)

Arguments

name

Unique identifier for the candidate. The four built-in names are reserved.

labels

One to six unique state labels, in increasing signature order.

formula

One-sided SSF formula. The default uses the canonical gamma terms, or only cos_angle if the fit specifies a length family. Supply angular and selection terms for a custom step-family formula. Assessment requires these terms in the fitted model; the fitted model may contain additional terms.

order_by

Name of a numeric movement metric from movement_metrics() (mean_step, sd_step, persistence, concentration, shape, or rate), or a function taking the unlabelled metrics and coefficient matrix and returning one score per state. Tied or non-finite scores fail the label assignment.

rules

Optional function of a single list containing metrics (rows named by label), coefficients and standard_errors (columns named by label), transition (rows and columns named by label), and occupancy (named by label). Its return value is a nonempty logical vector with unique names. Each FALSE or NA rejects the candidate. Standard errors are NA if the fit has no covariance matrix. The list also contains the joint natural-scale coefficient covariance and a parameter_index table identifying each row by state and term. Use ssf_contrast() to form a contrast without numeric parameter indices.

Value

An ssf_taxonomy specification for assess_taxonomy() and fit_guided_ssf().

Examples

ssf_taxonomy("step_regimes", c("Short steps", "Long steps"),
  rules = function(s) {
    c(length_ratio = s$metrics["Long steps", "mean_step"] >
        2 * s$metrics["Short steps", "mean_step"])
  })
#> $name
#> [1] "step_regimes"
#> 
#> $labels
#> [1] "Short steps" "Long steps" 
#> 
#> $formula
#> ~step + log_step + cos_angle
#> <environment: 0x10601e390>
#> 
#> $default_formula
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $order_by
#> [1] "mean_step"
#> 
#> $rules
#> function (s) 
#> {
#>     c(length_ratio = s$metrics["Long steps", "mean_step"] > 2 * 
#>         s$metrics["Short steps", "mean_step"])
#> }
#> <environment: 0x1060177e8>
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "ssf_taxonomy"
